senses.def: to tell the public about a product or service to persuade them to buy or use it
examples: The company spent millions advertising its new phone.
Cigarettes can no longer be advertised on TV.

senses.def: to make something publicly known, such as a job opening or an event
examples: The position was advertised online last week.
We advertised for a roommate on a local website.

note: American spelling ends in -ise, not -ize: advertise.

senses.def: a notice, picture or video that tells people about a product, job or service
examples: The magazine is full of advertisements for luxury watches.
She answered an advertisement for a part-time job.

note: American stress: ad-ver-TISE-ment. Everyday speech usually says "ad"; on TV/radio, "commercial".

senses.def: the activity or business of telling people about products and services to make them buy them
examples: She works in advertising for a firm in Manhattan.
The company cut its advertising budget this year.

note: Uncountable: "a lot of advertising", not "advertisings".

senses.def: an opinion or suggestion about what someone should do
examples: Can I give you a piece of advice?
You should get legal advice before signing the contract.

note: Uncountable: "some advice", "a piece of advice", never "an advice" or "advices". Noun advice /s/, verb advise /z/.

senses.def: to tell someone what you think they should do
examples: My doctor advised me to cut down on sugar.
I'd advise against driving in this snow.

senses.def: to give expert help on a subject, or formally to inform someone of something
examples: She advises the government on energy policy.
Passengers are advised that the flight is delayed.

senses.def: a person who publicly supports a particular idea, policy or group
examples: She is a passionate advocate for animal rights.
Advocates of the plan say it will create jobs.

senses.def: to publicly support or recommend a particular idea or course of action
examples: Many doctors advocate a plant-based diet.
The group advocates for better working conditions.

senses.def: a lawyer who defends someone in court
examples: The defendant was represented by a court-appointed advocate.

note: Pronunciation: noun /ˈædvəkət/, verb /ˈædvəkeɪt/. "Play devil's advocate" = argue the opposite side for discussion.

senses.def: connected with beauty, art and the appreciation of beautiful things
examples: The building has little aesthetic value.
Some people get cosmetic surgery for aesthetic reasons.

senses.def: a set of ideas or a style that controls how something looks
examples: The café has a minimalist aesthetic with white walls and wooden tables.

note: American English sometimes uses the spelling "esthetic". "Aesthetics" (noun) is the study of beauty.

senses.def: events or matters of public or political importance; usually plural
examples: She writes about foreign affairs for a major newspaper.
The minister refused to discuss the internal affairs of the party.

senses.def: an event or situation, often one that people talk about
examples: The whole affair has damaged his reputation.
The wedding was a small, family affair.

senses.def: a secret sexual relationship, especially when one person is married
examples: He admitted to having an affair with a coworker.

note: "That's my affair" = that's my business, not yours. "State of affairs" = the general situation.

senses.def: to cause a change in someone or something
examples: The new tax will affect millions of families.
Lack of sleep can affect your concentration.

senses.def: to make someone have strong feelings, especially sadness
examples: She was deeply affected by her father's death.

note: Affect is the verb; effect is usually the noun: "Stress affects health" / "Stress has an effect on health." Don't say "affect on".

senses.def: a feeling of liking or loving someone or something and caring about them
examples: He has a deep affection for his grandparents.
Cats show affection by rubbing against your legs.

senses.def: to have enough money to pay for something; usually with can, could or be able to
examples: We can't afford a new car right now.
Many young people can't afford to buy a home.

senses.def: to be able to do something without causing serious problems for yourself
examples: We can't afford to make any more mistakes.
I can't afford to take a day off this week.

note: Almost always with can/can't/could/be able to. Use "afford to do", not "afford doing".

senses.def: cheap enough for ordinary people to pay for
examples: The city badly needs more affordable housing.
The store sells stylish clothes at affordable prices.

senses.def: feeling fear, or worried that something bad might happen
examples: My little brother is afraid of the dark.
Don't be afraid to ask questions in class.

senses.def: used in "I'm afraid" to politely say something unpleasant or disappointing
examples: I'm afraid we're fully booked tonight.
"Is there any coffee left?" "I'm afraid not."

note: Not used before a noun: "the child was afraid", but "a frightened child" (not "an afraid child").

senses.def: later than something; following something in time or order
examples: Let's go for a walk after dinner.
Your name comes after mine on the list.

senses.def: at a time later than when something happens
examples: I'll call you after I finish work.
After she graduated, she moved to Seattle.

senses.def: later in time; afterward
examples: They lived happily ever after.
He got sick on Monday and died the week after.

senses.def: trying to find or catch someone, or named to honor someone
examples: The police are after him for robbery.
She was named after her grandmother.

note: After a conjunction, use present tense for future: "after I finish", not "after I will finish". "Look after" = take care of.

senses.tr: (kötü bir olayın) sonrası, ardından gelen durum
senses.def: the situation that follows an important, usually bad, event such as a war or disaster
examples: In the aftermath of the hurricane, thousands were left homeless.
The country struggled in the aftermath of the war.

note: Usually in the phrase "in the aftermath of"; it suggests something negative.

senses.def: the part of the day from about noon until about six in the evening
examples: I have a dentist appointment on Tuesday afternoon.
We spent the afternoon at the beach.

note: Use "in the afternoon" but "on Monday afternoon" and "this/yesterday afternoon" (no preposition).

senses.def: at a later time, after an event that has been mentioned
examples: We went to a movie and had dinner afterwards.
Shortly afterwards, the police arrived.

note: "Afterward" (without -s) is more common in American English; "afterwards" is more British.

senses.def: one more time, or on another occasion
examples: Could you say that again, please?
It's great to see you again!

senses.def: back to a previous place or condition
examples: She was happy to be home again after the long trip.
It took him weeks to feel healthy again.

note: "Then again" introduces a contrasting idea: "It's expensive. Then again, it's very good quality."

senses.def: opposing or disagreeing with someone or something
examples: Most residents are against the new airport.
It's against the law to text while driving.

senses.def: competing with an opponent, or protecting from something harmful
examples: We're playing against the best team in the league.
Get vaccinated against the flu every fall.

senses.def: touching or pressing on something, or hitting it
examples: He leaned his bike against the wall.
The rain beat against the windows all night.

note: Opposite in the "opinion" sense: "for" (Are you for or against the plan?).

senses.def: the number of years that a person has lived or a thing has existed
examples: She started playing the piano at the age of five.
Children under the age of 12 get in free.

senses.def: a particular period of history
examples: We live in the digital age.
The Bronze Age lasted for about 2,000 years.

senses.def: a very long time; used informally in the plural
examples: I haven't seen you for ages!
It took ages to find a parking space.

senses.def: to become older, or to make someone or something look or become older
examples: He has aged a lot since his wife died.
The wine is aged in oak barrels.

note: American spelling: aging (British: ageing).

senses.def: of a particular age
examples: The program is open to children aged 8 to 12.
The victim, a man aged 45, was taken to the hospital.

senses.def: very old; also "the aged" meaning old people as a group
examples: She takes care of her aged parents.
The center provides care for the aged.

note: Pronounced /eɪdʒd/ for "of the age of", but often /ˈeɪdʒɪd/ when it means "very old" (my aged parents).

senses.def: a business that provides a particular service, often for other companies or people
examples: We booked our trip through a travel agency.
She found her job through a recruitment agency.

senses.def: a government organization responsible for a particular area
examples: The Environmental Protection Agency issued new rules on air pollution.
Several federal agencies are investigating the case.

senses.def: a list of things to be discussed at a meeting
examples: The budget is the first item on the agenda.
Please send me the agenda before the meeting.

senses.def: a list of goals or issues that a person or group considers important, sometimes kept secret
examples: Health care is high on the president's agenda.
I think he has a hidden agenda.

note: False friend: an "agenda" is not a diary/planner (ajanda). For that, Americans say "planner" or "calendar".

senses.def: a person whose job is to act for or manage the business of other people
examples: Our real estate agent showed us five houses in one day.
The actor's agent negotiated a bigger salary.

senses.def: a person who works secretly for a government to get information
examples: FBI agents raided the office early in the morning.
He was a secret agent during the Cold War.

senses.def: a substance or thing that causes a change or has a particular effect
examples: Bleach is a powerful cleaning agent.

note: "Free agent" = a player or person free to sign with any team or do as they like.

senses.def: made up of many separate units combined together
examples: Aggregate demand fell sharply during the recession.
The study looks at aggregate data, not individual cases.

senses.def: a total formed by combining several separate amounts or things
examples: The team won 5–3 on aggregate over two games.
In the aggregate, the changes made a big difference.

senses.def: to combine different amounts or pieces of information into one total or group
examples: The website aggregates news stories from hundreds of sources.
The results were aggregated across all schools.

note: Formal/technical. Pronunciation: noun/adjective /ˈæɡrɪɡət/, verb /ˈæɡrɪɡeɪt/.

senses.def: angry feelings or threatening, violent behavior toward others
examples: Some dogs show aggression toward strangers.
Violent video games have been linked to aggression in children.

senses.def: an attack by one country on another without a good reason
examples: The invasion was condemned as an act of aggression.

senses.def: angry and behaving in a threatening way, ready to attack
examples: The man became aggressive when the bartender refused to serve him.
Keep away from that dog; it's aggressive.

senses.def: acting with determination and force to succeed or achieve a goal
examples: The company launched an aggressive marketing campaign.
Doctors chose an aggressive treatment for the tumor.

note: In business English, "aggressive" can be positive (bold, ambitious); compare "assertive" for confident but not hostile.

senses.def: used after a period of time to say how far back in the past something happened
examples: We moved to Denver five years ago.
I talked to her just a few minutes ago.

note: Use with the simple past, not the present perfect: "I saw him two days ago" (not "have seen"). Use "before" for earlier than a past time.

senses.def: to have the same opinion as someone
examples: I agree with you about the new design.
Most experts agree that exercise improves mental health.

senses.def: to say yes to a request or suggestion
examples: She agreed to help me move this weekend.

senses.def: to decide something together with someone after discussion
examples: The two sides finally agreed on a price.
We agreed to meet at noon.

note: "Agree" is a verb: say "I agree", not "I am agree" (a common Turkish-speaker error).

senses.def: an arrangement or contract made between people, groups or countries
examples: The two countries signed a trade agreement last month.
We have a verbal agreement, but nothing in writing.

senses.def: the state of having the same opinion
examples: We're all in agreement that the plan needs changes.
She nodded in agreement.

senses.def: connected with farming
examples: The region is famous for its agricultural products.
Much of the land is used for agricultural purposes.

senses.def: the science or work of farming, including growing crops and raising animals
examples: Agriculture is still the main source of income in the area.
Climate change poses a serious threat to agriculture.

senses.def: used to show surprise, pleasure, sympathy or sudden understanding
examples: Ah, so that's why the door was locked!
Ah, this coffee is exactly what I needed.

note: "Ah, well" expresses accepting something disappointing.

senses.def: further forward in space, or in front of someone
examples: There's a gas station a mile ahead.
She walked ahead of us, showing the way.

senses.def: in or into the future
examples: We have a busy week ahead.
It's important to plan ahead.

senses.def: winning or more advanced than others
examples: Our team was ahead by ten points at halftime.

note: "Go ahead" = devam et / buyur (permission). "Ahead of schedule" = earlier than planned.

senses.def: a serious illness caused by the HIV virus, which destroys the body's ability to fight infection
examples: New treatments have greatly reduced deaths from AIDS.
The charity funds AIDS research in Africa.

note: Short for Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. Always written in capital letters; Turkish uses the same abbreviation.

senses.def: money, food or other help given to countries or people in need
examples: The government sent emergency aid to the flood victims.
Most students at the college receive financial aid.

senses.def: a device or tool that helps you do something
examples: My grandfather wears a hearing aid.
Visual aids make a presentation easier to follow.

senses.def: to help someone or make something easier
examples: Fiber aids digestion.
The new software aids doctors in diagnosing cancer.

note: The verb is formal; in everyday speech use "help". "Aid" and "aide" (assistant) sound the same.

senses.def: a person who helps someone in an important job, especially a politician
examples: A senior White House aide spoke to reporters.
The senator's aides refused to comment.

senses.def: a person who assists a teacher, nurse or other professional
examples: She works as a teacher's aide at an elementary school.

senses.def: the purpose of doing something; what you hope to achieve
examples: The main aim of the project is to reduce waste.
She moved to New York with the aim of becoming an actress.

senses.def: to try or plan to achieve something
examples: We aim to finish the work by Friday.
The program is aimed at helping small businesses.

senses.def: to point a weapon or object at someone or something
examples: He aimed the camera at the stage and waited.

note: "Be aimed at" = intended for: "a book aimed at teenagers".

senses.def: the mixture of gases around the earth that we breathe
examples: Let's open a window and get some fresh air.
Air pollution is a major problem in big cities.

senses.def: the space above the ground, or travel by plane
examples: The kids threw their hats in the air.
Most of the goods are shipped by air.

senses.def: a particular feeling or quality that a person or place seems to have
examples: She has an air of confidence about her.

senses.def: to broadcast a program, or to let fresh air into a room
examples: The show airs every Sunday night at nine.

note: "On air" = being broadcast live. "Up in the air" = not yet decided.

senses.def: any vehicle that can fly, such as a plane or helicopter
examples: The airline has ordered fifty new aircraft.
A military aircraft crashed during a training exercise.

note: Plural is the same: one aircraft, two aircraft.

senses.def: a company that provides regular flights for passengers and goods
examples: The airline canceled dozens of flights because of the storm.
Which airline are you flying with?

senses.def: a place where planes take off and land, with buildings for passengers
examples: I'll pick you up at the airport at six.
We got to the airport two hours before our flight.

note: Say "at the airport" for location and "to the airport" for movement.

senses.def: a loud sound or device that warns people of danger or wakes them up
examples: The fire alarm went off in the middle of the night.
I set my alarm for 6:30.

senses.def: a sudden feeling of fear or worry that something bad might happen
examples: The news caused alarm among parents.
There's no cause for alarm.

senses.def: to make someone feel worried or afraid
examples: The rapid spread of the virus alarmed health officials.

senses.def: although; used to add something that makes the previous statement less strong
examples: The economy is growing, albeit slowly.
He accepted the offer, albeit with some reluctance.

note: Formal. Usually followed by an adjective, adverb or phrase, not a full clause.

senses.def: a collection of songs released together as one recording
examples: The band's new album comes out next month.
It's one of the best-selling albums of all time.

senses.def: a book with empty pages for keeping photos, stamps or similar things
examples: My mom keeps all our baby pictures in a photo album.

senses.def: drinks such as beer, wine and whiskey that can make people drunk
examples: You must be 21 to buy alcohol in the United States.
He stopped drinking alcohol two years ago.

senses.def: a clear liquid used in drinks, medicines and cleaning products
examples: Clean the cut with rubbing alcohol.

senses.def: containing alcohol, or connected with alcohol
examples: The bar also serves non-alcoholic cocktails.
Alcoholic drinks are not allowed in the park.

senses.def: a person who is addicted to alcohol
examples: His father was an alcoholic who never sought help.

senses.def: able to think quickly and notice things; watching carefully for danger
examples: Coffee helps me stay alert during long drives.
Drivers should stay alert for deer on this road.

senses.def: a warning about danger, or a situation in which people watch for danger
examples: Police are on high alert after the threats.
I got a news alert on my phone about the earthquake.

senses.def: to warn someone about a danger or a situation that needs action
examples: A neighbor alerted the police after hearing screams.

senses.def: a creature from another planet
examples: The movie is about aliens who invade Earth.
Do you believe aliens have visited our planet?

senses.def: (formal or legal) a person who is not a citizen of the country where they live
examples: Legal aliens must carry their green card at all times.

senses.def: strange, unfamiliar and sometimes frightening
examples: The idea of working from home was alien to my parents.
Life in the city felt alien to him at first.

note: "Illegal alien" is considered offensive by many; "undocumented immigrant" is now common.

senses.def: to arrange things in a straight line or in the correct position relative to each other
examples: Align the text to the left side of the page.
The mechanic aligned the front wheels.

senses.tr: uyumlu hale getirmek; (align with) safında yer almak
senses.def: to change something so it matches something else, or to publicly support a group
examples: We need to align our budget with our goals.
The party aligned itself with the labor unions.
